title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: In *Scholar of the First Sin*, Aldia, the older brother of King Vendrick, hints at a path for the Bearer of the Curse that differs from the one presented to them. If the conditions are met, he can serve as the final boss of *Dark Souls II*, with his fight triggering after Nashandra's; he, notably, is the only boss in any *Dark Souls* game not to die when defeated, and as such drops no souls nor items, with the player instead gaining the option of an alternate ending in which the Bearer of the Curse is hinted to as following this mysterious other path at Aldia's side. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via the Soul Stream description, which refers to him as "**the first of the Scholars**". He is voiced by David Gant, who also voiced Oswald of Carim in *Dark Souls*.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : Aldia serves as a lore-centric character, alluding to a great deal of things in relation to the lore of *Dark Souls II*.

When the Bearer of the Curse has defeated the Four Great Ones and lit the Primal Bonfires he will emerge and guide the Bearer of the Curse towards his brother Vendrick, now a mindless hollow. He continues to appear to the Bearer of the Curse, seeking to learn their intentions and telling them of the nature of the curse and the fabric of their world.

He will finally attack the Bearer of the Curse before they can take the Throne of Want, seeking to test them. When Aldia is defeated, he will ask what the Bearer of the Curse wants: light, dark or something else entirely. If the Bearer of the Curse chooses to reject the throne and leave, Aldia will narrate the Bearer of the Curse's departure from the throne.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

The Scholar asks of the Bearer to seek Vendrick, "he who almost became a true monarch", for he will guide their way.  strategy : Aldia is immobile when fought, but is able to teleport, releasing an area of effect attack around the area he teleports to.

Several of Aldia's attacks deal mixed Fire and Dark damage, so some form of fire defense is recommended for this fight. All of his attacks deal either pure physical or Fire/Dark damage. The Fire Orbs have moderate tracking, so rolling may be needed to fully evade. Forbidden Sun can be cast in any direction, even directly behind him. The Fire Orb and Forbidden Sun attacks can be avoided by rolling, strafing around Aldia or running perpendicular to their trajectory.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

title: Deacons of the Deep
snippet: When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: The Deep
snippet: Leaving Archdeacon Royce and the main clergy to keep watch over the Cathedral and their saint's coffin, Aldrich marched with McDonnell and his clerics on Irithyll, defying the orders of Sulyvahn himself. Forcing his way through the city's barrier, he slaughtered the Pontiff's Knights, and forced him to allow Aldrich access to the old Cathedral of Anor Londo, where the Dark Sun Gwyndolin was imprisoned. Taking residence in the old Cathedral, Aldrich took the first step to bringing about the Age of Deep Sea, and began feasting on the helpless God of the Darkmoon.

title: Carim
snippet: At least one of the priests of Velka, Goddess of Sin came from Carim. He wore a uniformly black attire and wielded an enchanted blade both infused with the mystical power of Velka. His mission as a "pardoner" was to listen to the confessions of humans that sinned against the gods, urging reflection but also offering salvation and pardoning them of their sins. The pardoner seemed to have no problem selling the "Bite" rings, whose creation process was highly questionable, or Velka's rings crafted through the sacrificial rites in the name of his goddess.

Eating people became a routine for Aldrich, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Having accumulated immense knowledge through his vast, twisted experiments, Aldia directed his research towards infusing the qualities of the everlasting dragons into humans, to free them from the shackles of their fleeting form and transcend, like the followers of the Dragon Remnants were trying to do using stones infused with the power of the dragons. The scholar obtained some of the Giants that his brother had captured and kept them in his manor as experimental subjects in an attempt to use their bodies and souls to recreate a dragon, only producing creatures with bones resembling draconic features that were killed once they had outlived their usefulness. His sustained efforts resulted in humans that turned into half-dragons, transformed into undead aberrations with deformed skulls that became close to those of the dragons but still degraded into hollows.

title: First sin
snippet: The term "First Sin" is likely derived from the Judeo-Christian account of humankind's [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_sin original sin], generally agreed amongst most sects to be a base flaw in all people stemming from the original humans, Adam and Eve, partaking in the fruits of a certain tree in the Garden of Eden; the sole action God strictly forbade that they do under threat of death. This fruit opened their eyes, allowing them to see and "be as God, knowing good and evil", but in disobeying God they effectively caused humans to be branded by Him as untrustworthy and capable of sin. He then cast them out of the Garden and had them toil for their food all their lives. Most significantly, however, was that there was a second tree within the Garden that bestowed everlasting life, with God Himself saying "and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever" before casting the pair out to eventually die.

snippet: The Sable Church of Londor revere the Unkindled, as it is prophesied that an Unkindled will become the Lord of Hollows and bring about the Age of Dark. Elfriede, the eldest of the three sisters of the Sable Church, eventually departed Londor and attempted to link the Flame. The circumstances surrounding her departure are unclear; whether she intended to usurp the Flame or wholly abandoned Londor is uncertain. Regardless, she was unable to link the Flame, burned to Unkindled Ash. After her resurrection, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, a safe haven for the forlorn and the misshapen.

title: The Deep
snippet: At his new posting at the Cathedral, Aldrich was provided a steady flow of sustenance in the form of the Road of Sacrifices. The Cathedral would dispatch Evangelists to establish missions and gain influence at the Undead Settlement; these preachers would tell stories of enlightenment to the cursed Undead, who were shipped off en masse to become feed to Aldrich's gluttony. At some point, he would desire for others to share in the elation of devouring men; to this end he fashioned warped magic rings that allowed one to feel the same depraved sensations as the repulsive maneater. The bearers of these rings mutated into accursed bestial creatures with stomachs filled with the remains of their meals.

snippet: The Scholar alludes to the fates of the three kings, whether or not the player has played through *The Lost Crowns* DLCs. title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
**Tree Root Dance**:

Aldia slams a root into the ground, causing numerous tree roots to protrude from the ground, moving towards the player rapidly. Just like the Fire Snake pyromancy. **How to avoid:** the roots start appearing right in front of Aldia at the center; a root never appears twice in the same location. Knowing this, first stand closer to his left or right side to avoid the initial roots, then quickly move to stand right in front of him, where the first roots appeared, and the other roots won't be able to follow you.

**Circular Tree Root Dance**:

Aldia slams a root into the ground, causing numerous tree roots to come out of the ground around him, not moving towards the player. **How to avoid:** watch the fire patches appearing on the ground before the roots and move away from them.

**Teleport:**

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
**Teleport:**

Aldia can teleport at any time. Upon finishing a teleport, he emits an area of effect attack immediately. **How to avoid:** watch the red light that appears at the location where Aldia is teleporting, then stand back to avoid the blast (similar to Smelter Demon's fire blast). After that immediately run up to him to land a few hits before his flames go up.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
The withered tree branches he utilizes inflict physical damage only, making them especially prone to being blocked. At a distance, the branches extend out of the ground in a path in front of him, with moderate tracking, making it harder to roll out of the path of the attack. This is easily noted when one rolls away from the attack, but gets grazed by one of the branches, yet doesn't flinch or stagger upon getting hit.

Throughout the fight, Aldia will surround himself in a fiery aura that makes close contact with him difficult without the risk of dying to the flames. However, an ultra greatsword can still reach. This aura also bolsters his own defenses, reducing the damage he receives from all attacks by a significant amount. The fiery aura fades when he performs certain moves, giving the player a small window to attack up close. The first opening is just after he teleports to a new location, and the second is when he is charging up his Forbidden Sun attack.

snippet:
Xbox One, PS4 and DirectX 11 versions of the game include the following features in addition to those listed above:
Additional upgrades to graphics, sound and performance.
Increase in maximum online players in a single session (6 total).
A complete revamp of character, enemy and item placement, which gives players a new experience.
The Forlorn will hunt the player down throughout their journey. Their equipment can also be acquired by the player. These items include their Armor, Greatsword and Scythe.

title: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Increased effect of Rusted Coin.
The bonfire warp selection screen will now highlight the top three areas where players will have the best chance to connect with other players online.
Players on their first playthrough can now match with players on their 2nd or further playthroughs.
Made it so that invading players cannot use items which invite more enemies.
NPC conversation texts are now displayed more prominently than online notices.
Players may now choose to cancel out the effect of the Human Effigy at bonfires.
Calibrations no longer saved each time before the title screen.
Made it possible to skip the ending sequence the 2nd time through and beyond.
Adjusted timing for Licia of Lindeldt to become the player's enemy.
To prevent invasion after defeating area bosses, made the Human Effigy effect function in this situation automatically.
In Black Gulch, made it possible to receive the Forgotten Key after defeating a Giant when the player has 99 Souls of a Giant.

Upon coming to the final rope bridge, the player may first opt to use the zip-line to unlock the shortcut to and from the bonfire before proceeding across the bridge.
**In *Scholar of the First Sin*, the shortcut is open from the start, allowing the player to skip the entire area and proceed directly to the Dragon Shrine. Additionally, a petrified enemy requiring a Fragrant Branch of Yore to be bypassed has been added to the first bridge.
Remaining stagnant on the bridge leading up to the Dragon Shrine for too long will cause the dragon to come down and crush the bridge.

snippet:
Dragon Aerie -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : Dragon Aerie is a rather short area, with only one bonfire. Located high above the surface of the earth, numerous columns of rock, connected by rope bridges, are home to the kin of the Guardian Dragon fought at Aldia's Keep. Each of the dragon nests harbors numerous Crystal Lizards that drop Titanite Chunks, Slabs, Twinkling Titanites and Petrified Dragon Bones, among other stones.

snippet:
Dragon Aerie -  Dark Souls II - location - plot 
 plot : After defeating the Guardian Dragon in Aldia's Keep, the player makes their way through the Dragon Aerie in order to reach the Dragon Shrine and receive the Ashen Mist Heart. The player will have to navigate across swaying bridges, and watch their footing around perilous cliffsides and sudden drops.
